passage:
Mina found her grandfather's old passport in a drawer. The pages were full of stamps from countries she had never visited.
Her grandfather explained that he had worked on ships when he was young. Each stamp marked a port, but not all memories were happy. Some trips were lonely. Some were dangerous. Some changed how he saw home.
Mina had thought travel was mostly about taking photos and buying gifts. The passport showed another side: work, distance, and adaptation.
The small booklet made the world feel larger and her grandfather's life deeper.
A passport records movement, but the real journey lives in the person who carried it.
